analysis.title: Microsoft Corporation 1Q27 Preview: Azure growth and a growing focus on the enterprise AI stack
key_insights: BofA reiterates Buy and $600 PO on MSFT (price $531.87). The PO is based on 28x CY27E P/E, a premium to the 18-25x peer group. Stock is up about 33% since the 4Q26 report, which showed 43% Azure growth.
MSFT reports 1Q27 results on Oct. 28, 2026. BofA models revenue of $90.6bn (+16.6% YoY) and EPS of $4.73, both in line with Street.

Under the new reporting structure, MSFT reports two segments, Agents & Infrastructure and Devices & Consumers, and discloses Azure revenue in dollars for the first time. The narrower Azure definition excludes GitHub and Security Copilot.
BofA expects Azure to grow 44.8% YoY cc to $32.3bn in 1Q27 and 45.1% cc in 2Q27, broadly in line with Street. The model has Azure at 44.3% growth for FY27.

Azure growth is supported by about 1GW of data center capacity added per quarter, which supports conversion of the $678bn commercial RPO into revenue. MSFT remains on track to roughly double total capacity by CY28.

Execution levers on Azure: GPU deployment times in the largest regions were cut by nearly 50% over the past year, and Copilot workload throughput rose 4x since the start of the year. Fairwater's first Wisconsin facility came online in April, six weeks ahead of schedule.
MSFT plans to deploy Maia 300 in CY27, expected to deliver 40% more tokens per megawatt than leading GPU systems, which should improve inference economics.
BofA models 1Q27 capex including finance leases of $50.8bn, up 24% QoQ, and FY27 capex of $220.7bn, up 51.9% YoY. FY27 FCF margin is modeled at 7.5%, down 12.7 percentage points YoY.

The redesigned Copilot combines chat, delegated work (Cowork), application building (Code) and AI agents (Autopilot) in one interface, connected to company data through Fabric IQ. BofA views it as the operating layer for enterprise AI.

Copilot pricing: everyday tasks stay in the $30 fixed-price M365 Copilot subscription, while Cowork, Code and Autopilot consume usage-based Copilot Credits layered on top of the per-seat model, a path to higher ARPU.
Paid Copilot seats rose from 15mn in 2Q26 to 20mn in 3Q26 and 30mn in 4Q26, with net additions more than doubling QoQ in 4Q26. BofA says continued seat momentum is needed to support the stock.

BofA's CIO survey (n=309): 76.7% use or plan to use Copilot in production, ahead of AI labs and Google Gemini at 30.4%. 69.3% expect to raise security spending with Microsoft, versus CrowdStrike at 35.6%. 88.4% of respondents investing in cloud AI are likely to use Microsoft, versus AWS at 72.2%.
91.2% of survey respondents increased AI compute use over the past 12 months and 54.0% increased it significantly, supporting BofA's view that Azure demand exceeds supply through FY27.
BofA raises estimates: FY27 EPS to $19.70 from $19.55, FY28 to $23.43 from $22.89, FY29 to $28.49 from $27.61. FY27 revenue goes to $391.9bn from $388.5bn.
Devices & Consumers revenue is modeled down 6.2% in 1Q27 on continued Xbox weakness. 1Q27 operating margin is modeled at 48.4%; FY27 operating margin at 46.4%, down 20bps YoY.

market_movers.rationale: Azure acceleration, Copilot monetization and improving visibility into AI investment returns. PO is 28x CY27E P/E.

sector_views.rationale: Enterprise AI becomes the top IT priority for 2027 and Microsoft is positioned across applications, security and infrastructure.

earnings_insights: MSFT 1Q27 results due Oct. 28, 2026. BofA estimates (not reported): revenue $90.6bn (Bloomberg consensus $90.6459bn), GAAP EPS $4.73 vs consensus $4.72, operating margin 48.4% vs consensus 48.3%.
BofA estimates for 1Q27 Azure revenue $32.26bn, +44.1% YoY and +44.8% cc, vs consensus $32.24bn and 44.8% cc. 2Q27 Azure est. $34.9bn, +45.1% cc, vs consensus 45.0%.
BofA estimates for 1Q27 capex including leases of $50.8bn vs consensus $51.8bn (-1.9%). FY27 capex est. $220.7bn vs consensus $218.6bn.
BofA estimates for 1Q27 Agents & Infrastructure revenue $75.6bn (+22.6% YoY), M365 Cloud $27.5bn (+15.9%) and Devices & Consumers $15.0bn (-6.2%), all in line with consensus.
BofA estimates for 2Q27 total revenue $95.8bn (+17.8% cc) and GAAP EPS $4.84, in line with consensus $4.84. FY27 EPS est. $19.70 vs Bloomberg consensus $19.76.
risk_factors: Near-term gross margin pressure as Azure grows as a share of revenue.
AI applications and model providers could innovate faster than Microsoft, limiting its growth profile.
Enterprise application spending is cyclical and discretionary.
Azure revenue conversion depends on delivering compute capacity; capacity additions are the key variable.
Elevated capex pushes FY27 FCF down 56.3% to $29.3bn in BofA's model.
charts_described: Exhibit 1: Share of CIO survey respondents using or planning to use AI models: Microsoft Copilot 76.7%, AI labs 66.9%, Google Gemini 30.4%, open-weight third-party models 12.6%, other 7.1%.
Exhibit 2: Cybersecurity vendors expected to see the greatest spending increases: Microsoft 69.3%, CrowdStrike 35.6%, Palo Alto 22.3%, Okta 21.0%.
Exhibit 3: Azure revenue estimates of $32,255mn, $34,915mn, $37,530mn and $42,360mn for 1Q27E to 4Q27E, with YoY cc growth of 44.8%, 45.1%, 44.7% and 43.4%.
Exhibit 4: Azure revenue of $101,938mn in FY26, $147,060mn in FY27E and $207,852mn in FY28E, with growth of 40.4%, 44.3% and 41.3%.
